title: Lucky Thompson's quarrel with Gladys at the Famous Door in 1943
summary: Lucky Thompson, cocky after three years on the horn, asks Gladys to pay for a new horn, and after the Famous Door engagement ends over unpaid wages he and his wife curse her.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, on that (inaudible) was Lucky Thompson in those days? This is --
Lucky been playing about three years when he come with Hamp's band and could play very good for three years. He come out of Wilberforce University in Ohio. But very cocky.

And he had gotten to the point, and it was a hassle that he and Hamp was -- no reason at all, and I wasn't guilty of the fact that what had happened. He had wanted a new horn, and he had gone to Gladys and asked Gladys to pay for the horn. He'd pay her back, and she said, okay,

man, I'll do that.

We were at this time, in 1943, in the Famous Door in New York, and the night that we opened up there, they had Benny Goodman, had all the stars, Billy Eckstine, Lena Horne, Georgia Auld, Duke Ellington, Louis Armstrong. I mean the works. That opening night was terrific. I blew my neck off my horn on Flying Home. I could (inaudible) I blew it off. So my horn was damaged. I had to rubber band it down and everything in the middle of the show. So I couldn't go downstairs and hit no low notes. So I had to stay uptown with it until I got through.

Now, Lucky is giving Gladys a fit, and his wife joins in after we get into a situation, and Gladys ain't getting no money at the end of the week. We had two weeks up there. We didn't make the second. We didn't make the second week because they had trouble.

Then Lucky's going to needle her for his horn.
Well, what kind of trouble happened?
What kind of trouble was it? Why didn't you make the second week?
Gladys had a hassle with her money. You know, when she started to having a hassle with money, she cut you off. And needling, you can forget it. That was her principle, and she lived on it.
And Lucky chose a time like that --

But his wife joined in, and they all cussed Gladys out, both of them. So Gladys forgot him. Now, I'm having trouble with my horn. Lucky comes up to the Audubon Ballroom up on 166th Street and Audubon, near the Medical Center. And he done sold his horn and come to play Hamp's job with a clarinet. And Hamp said, ch-ch-ch-ch (inaudible). He said, well, I'm going to play clarinet until I get my tenor.
